newsitem.title: USA: US T-bond futures end lower after staging rally.
newsitem.headline: US T-bond futures end lower after staging rally.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended narrowly mixed, with T-bond contracts finishing on the downside as traders and dealers booked profits after December rose above a key resistance level at midsession, they said.

Profit-taking in the T-bond futures pit gained momentum after one wire service quoted San Francisco Federal Reserve president Robert Parry as saying inflationary pressures could worsen, several floor traders said.
December bonds, which eased off nine-month highs at 116-05/32 earlier in the day, turned negative, while March Eurodollars EDH7 stabilized at the upper end of ranges.
The 1.0-percent decline in Redbook's weekly retail sales index for the first three weeks of fiscal November versus October was unable to firm December bonds into the close.

Traders are awaiting for several major U.S. economic reports on Thursday. Reports like the revised third-quarter Gross Domestic Product, October durable goods and weekly U.S. jobless claims should provide the market with more direction, traders said.
Eurodollars have perfectly priced in a moderate-growth, low-inflation scenario that recent U.S. economics reports have indicated.
Any indications that the U.S. economic growth is slowing in the fourth-quarter could lift March Eurodollars to 94.57, an Elliott Wave target, one analyst said.
December bonds could test 116-11/32, which is a two-thirds retracement level from the 10-1/2-month downmove.
"There is a lot of goodness priced into the market right now," one analyst said.

December bonds rallied through the 62-percent Fibonacci retracement level of 115-29/32 after the U.S. consumer confidence report was at 107.3, lower than average trade estimates of 109.00 and against October's 107.3.
Analysts also attributed December's spike higher to fund managers re-adjusting their portfolios.

Traders said there were heavy amounts of spread trading, as positions in December were rolled into March USH7. March becomes lead contract month during the CBOT's evening session on Sunday. The last trading day for December is on Thursday, December 19.
Several firms alone each rolled about 2,000 contracts into March, floor traders said. Within the first two hours of trade, about 40,000 spreads had traded.
Thin pit conditions are expected for the rest of the week, as a majority of traders make a long U.S. holiday weekend out of the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.

Both Eurodollar and bond pits will be shut on Thursday, and will close early on Wednesday and Friday. Eurodollars will end at 1200 CST/1800 GMT on those days, while T-bond and notes futures will shut at 1210 CST/1810 GMT.

At the end of pit trade, December T-bonds were off 04/32 at 115-11/32, 10-year notes were steady at 110-30/32, March Eurodollars were up one basis point at 94.51, and June Eurodollars were also up a bps at 94.42.
